clue.text: Is this what unrefined little girls are made of?

definitions.text: Is this what unrefined little girls are made of?

parts.words: Is this what unrefined little girls are made of?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme says little girls are made of sugar and spice; the unrefined form of sugar is a dark syrup, and LASSES (girls) sits inside it

explanation.surface: A tease about the old rhyme on what little girls are made of, asking about rough, unpolished ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme says girls are 'sugar and spice'; unrefined girls would be made of the unrefined by-product of sugar, and the word conveniently ends in LASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle-like syrup left over from refining sugar is the sugary stuff in its crude, unrefined state.

clue.text: Given too much bread, proved Al as it turned out

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters of proved and Ai are turned into a new order

parts.note: the printed words, with Al read as Ai, the letters the anagram needs

explanation.surface: Someone named Al proved to have been paid too much.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed 'Al' gives an L the answer lacks; the anagram needs AI. 'Bread' is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, so being handed too much of it is to be paid more than you earned.

clue.text: Light buffer's hollow place is fabulous!

definitions.text: Light buffer's hollow place is fabulous!

parts.note: the boy in the tale who rubbed (buffed) a magic lamp to summon a genie
a hollow place in rock is a cave

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the den of someone who polishes lamps is marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' is a lamp and its 'buffer' the boy from the Arabian Nights who rubbed it; 'fabulous' is both 'wonderful' and 'from a fable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The treasure-filled cavern of the folk tale has become an idiom for any place crammed with wonderful things.

clue.text: Thinly-spread butter and pickle

definitions.meaning: a scraping of butter is a very thin layer
a pickle is an awkward predicament, a fix

explanation.definitionFit: A mean layer of butter is a thin smear, and a tight spot or awkward predicament is also a fix.

clue.text: Catch made from two metals

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A hook or clasp forged from a pair of metals.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden drawback, the catch in a deal.

clue.text: Standard delight, say-or a bit of it

indicators.note: say tells us the words are spoken and give a sound-alike

parts.note: par is a standard or norm, and to tickle is to delight

explanation.surface: Some standard pleasure, or only a small portion of it.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR (standard) plus TICKLE (delight) spoken together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny fragment or speck of something.

clue.text: Jetty ripe for renovation

indicators.note: renovation means the letters of ripe are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A landing stage ready to be done up.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetty is a structure built out into the water for boats to moor at.

clue.text: Clergyman always in Split we hear

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
we hear points to a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
ever means always

explanation.surface: A churchman who is always in two minds, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns RENT (a split) into its sound-alike REND, and 'in' places EVER inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title and informal name for a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Low water in Dee, apt to swirl

indicators.note: swirling water stirs the letters of in, Dee and apt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The shallows of the River Dee, inclined to eddy about.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river, which helps the watery picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap tide is the tide of least range, with the lowest high water of the lunar month.

clue.text: She was visited by a swan, lead-damaged

definitions.text: She was visited by a swan

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of lead are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: A woman a swan called on, roughed up by lead.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Zeus came to the queen of Sparta disguised as a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Zeus took the form of a swan to seduce this Spartan queen.

clue.text: Brewers' delivery animal?

parts.note: brewers pulled beer, served from the cask, to pubs with heavy cart horses; a cart horse is named after both pulling and beer from the tap

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy horse bred for pulling loads was the traditional means of delivering barrels from brewery to pub.

clue.text: This cocktail is not with it

definitions.meaning: a whisky cocktail made with bitters, sugar and orange peel
not with it means out of date, behind the times

explanation.definitionFit: A classic bourbon cocktail bears this name, and someone behind the times is out of touch with fashion.

clue.text: Easily-seen cargo-list?

definitions.meaning: a ship's document listing its freight

explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious is plain for all to see, and a ship's document itemising its freight is a list of goods carried.

clue.text: First at Thirsk-"Game Way"-certainty!

indicators.note: first at takes only the opening letter of the word Thirsk

parts.note: RU is rugby union
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A tip at Thirsk races: the horse Game Way is a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirsk is a racecourse in North Yorkshire, so the surface reads as a racing tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust is firm confidence, an assured reliance on something.

clue.text: Way to cook eggs (divine, wrapped in cabbage)

indicators.note: wrapped in means one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: cole is an old word for cabbage
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a divine

explanation.surface: A heavenly egg recipe in which the eggs come wrapped in cabbage leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a noun, a clergyman, abbreviated DD.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle eggs is to cook them gently in water just below boiling.

clue.text: Bad day for some of the side-issues

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Bad day for some of the side-issues' (IDES): 'some of' signals a hidden word, but the printed words hold IDEI, not IDES, and no other parse gives IDES without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Bad day for some of the side-issues

clue.text: Crude style in swirling mist

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
swirling stirs the letters of mist into a new order

parts.note: mode means style or fashion

explanation.surface: An unrefined fashion seen in the swirling fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' turns MIST into IMST, and 'in' puts MODE inside it as IM-MODE-ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodest behaviour is indecent or vulgar, which is to say crude.

clue.text: Doctor to deal with black-eye

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
to use something is to deal with it

explanation.surface: A doctor called in to treat a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouse' is old slang for a black eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse is slang for a bruised, swollen eye, from its dark colour and rounded shape.

clue.text: Humidity of our times controlled?

indicators.note: controlled means the letters of our times are managed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether the dampness of the modern age is kept in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the air, its dampness.

clue.text: Lincoln died-but not here, peacefully?

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln died, but not quietly at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln was shot in a theatre, not in his bed; dying peacefully would be in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in bed is the setting for a peaceful death, as opposed to dying somewhere else.

clue.text: Wind that blows Daisy in cathedral?

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A breeze blowing a daisy about inside a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a name but is a flower, ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind coming from the east.

clue.text: Law-breaking month abroad in African republic

indicators.note: breaking means law breaks into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: Mai is French for May, a month abroad
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lawbreaking in a far-off month in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law-breaking' looks like crime, but LAW breaks into MAI, French for May.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked republic in south-east Africa.

clue.text: Case of pine in river

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire
to pine is to long for, to ache

explanation.surface: A box made of pine sitting in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like wood for a case, but is the verb, to long for.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a large wooden box for shipping tea, often used later for packing.

clue.text: Silver pin that can damage the index, for example

definitions.text: that can damage the index, for example

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a nail is a metal pin

explanation.surface: A silver pin that could injure an index finger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'index' is the forefinger; an agnail is a hangnail.
explanation.definitionFit: A torn strip of skin beside a fingernail can make the forefinger sore.

clue.text: Piece in Verdi motet out of tune?

indicators.note: out of tune suggests the letters of in, Verdi and motet are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A section of a Verdi choral work sung off key.
explanation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light piece of music, usually for a small ensemble.

clue.text: From very opening to close-sell!

indicators.note: opening takes only the first letter of the word very

parts.note: close means end

explanation.surface: A trader's motto: sell, from start to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To vend is to offer goods for sale.

clue.text: Fancy some of my therapy?

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question whether a little of the treatment is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy here is an invention of the imagination, a fiction.

clue.text: Band's adversary jolly average!

parts.note: Yes is a rock band, and the opposite of yes is no
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: The opponent of a musical group is jolly ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes was a British progressive rock band; 'jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: The norm is the usual or typical level, the average.

clue.text: Ornament, appreciated by…

parts.note: an ornament with rays, and a break in the clouds that the people in the next clue on their break would welcome

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue: a burst of sun is appreciated by those on a break.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooch or design of rays spreading from a centre is named after the sun breaking through cloud.

clue.text: Henry visiting lido, say, for a break?

definitions.text: Henry visiting lido, say, for a break?

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: break suggests the letters of lido and say are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Henry goes to the open-air pool for some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' is the unit H, not a man; the whole clue describes time off at the lido.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the seaside pool for some time off work is a vacation.
